title: Bharata beholds Rama's hermitage and approaches it
introduction: Bharata observes various signs, proving Rama's hermitage in the vicinity of his place of search. After proceeding for a distance, Bharata beholds Rama's hermitage and Rama too seated in the hut, wearing matted locks. Bharata laments on Rama's misfortune of living as an ascetic Bharata and Shatrughna throw themselves on Rama's feet in salutation. Rama embraces them both.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे एकोनशततमः सर्गः
Thus completes 99th Chapter of Ayodhya Kanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
निविष्टायाम् तु सेनायाम् उत्सुको भरतः तदा |
जगाम भ्रातरम् द्रष्टुम् शत्रुघ्नम् अनुदर्शयन्
verses.iast:
niviṣṭāyām tu senāyām utsuko bharataḥ tadā |
jagāma bhrātaram draṣṭum śatrughnam anudarśayan
verses.translation: Having stationed his forces, Bharata set out eagerly to see his brother, pointing out the sign of Rama's habitation to Shatrughna.

glosses.meaning: pointing out (the sign of Rama's habitation)

verses.devanagari:
ऋषिम् वसिष्ठम् संदिश्य मातृऋर् मे शीघ्रम् आनय |
इति तरितम् अग्रे स जागम गुरु वत्सलः
verses.iast:
ṛṣim vasiṣṭham saṃdiśya mātṛṛr me śīghram ānaya |
iti taritam agre sa jāgama guru vatsalaḥ
verses.translation: Bharata, who was affectionate towards the elders, asked the sage Vasishta to bring his mothers soon thereafter and went ahead quickly.

glosses.meaning: who was affectionate towards the elders

verses.devanagari:
सुमन्त्रः तु अपि शतुघ्नम् अदूराद् अन्वपद्यत |
राम दार्शनजः तर्षो भरतस्य इव तस्य च
verses.iast:
sumantraḥ tu api śatughnam adūrād anvapadyata |
rāma dārśanajaḥ tarṣo bharatasya iva tasya ca
verses.translation: Sumantra also, equally desirous of seeing Rama; followed Shatrughna at a little distance.

verses.devanagari:
गग्च्छन्न् एव अथ भरतः तापस आलय संस्थिताम् |
भ्रातुः पर्ण कुटीम् श्रीमान् उटजम् च ददर्श ह
verses.iast:
gagcchann eva atha bharataḥ tāpasa ālaya saṃsthitām |
bhrātuḥ parṇa kuṭīm śrīmān uṭajam ca dadarśa ha
verses.translation: While the illustrious Bharata passed on, he observed in that wood of ascetics, a leafy hut of his brother together with a small hut made of leaves, nearby.

glosses.meaning: and a (small) hut made of leaves nearby
situated in that wood of ascestics.

verses.devanagari:
शालायाः तु अग्रतः तस्या ददर्श भरतः तदा |
काष्टानि च अवभग्नानि पुष्पाण्य् अवचितानि च
verses.iast:
śālāyāḥ tu agrataḥ tasyā dadarśa bharataḥ tadā |
kāṣṭāni ca avabhagnāni puṣpāṇy avacitāni ca
verses.translation: Bharata then beheld wood that had been broken up and heaps of flowers gathered in front of that hermitage.

verses.devanagari:
स लक्ष्मणस्य रामस्य ददर्शाश्रममीयुषः |
कृतं वृक्षेष्वभिज्ञानं कुशचीरैः क्वचित् क्वचित्
verses.iast:
sa lakśmaṇasya rāmasya dadarśāśramamīyuṣaḥ |
kṛtaṃ vṛkṣeṣvabhijJṇānaṃ kuśacīraiḥ kvacit kvacit
verses.translation: While coming to the hermitage, Bharata saw some signs here and there serving as a proper direction to that hermitage, tufts of Kusha grass and strips of bark tied to the trees by Rama and Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: as signs serving as a proper direction to their hermitage
tufts of Kusha grass and strips of bark

verses.devanagari:
स ददर्श वने तस्मिन् महतः संचयान् कृतान् |
मृगाणाम् महिषाणाम् च करीषैः शीत कारणात्
verses.iast:
sa dadarśa vane tasmin mahataḥ saṃcayān kṛtān |
mṛgāṇām mahiṣāṇām ca karīṣaiḥ śīta kāraṇāt
verses.translation: Bharata also saw in the vicinity great heaps of dried dung of deers and buffaloes, kept ready for protection against cold.

verses.devanagari:
गग्च्छन् एव महा बाहुर् द्युतिमान् भरतः तदा |
शत्रुघ्नम् च अब्रवीद्द् हृष्टः तान् अमात्यामः च सर्वशः
verses.iast:
gagcchan eva mahā bāhur dyutimān bharataḥ tadā |
śatrughnam ca abravīdd hṛṣṭaḥ tān amātyāmḥ ca sarvaśaḥ
verses.translation: Then, proceeding further, the valiant and the mighty armed Bharata spoke to Shatrughna in joy, as also those ministers who surrounded him.

verses.devanagari:
मन्ये प्राप्ताः स्म तम् देशम् भरद्वाजो यम् अब्रवीत् |
न अतिदूरे हि मन्ये अहम् नदीम् मन्दाकिनीम् इतः
verses.iast:
manye prāptāḥ sma tam deśam bharadvājo yam abravīt |
na atidūre hi manye aham nadīm mandākinīm itaḥ
verses.translation: "I think we have reached the place about which Bharadwaja directed us. I believe Mandakini River is not far from here."

verses.devanagari:
उच्चैर् बद्धानि चीराणि लक्ष्मणेन भवेद् अयम् |
अभिज्नान कृतः पन्था विकाले गन्तुम् इग्च्छता
verses.iast:
uccair baddhāni cīrāṇi lakṣmaṇena bhaved ayam |
abhijnāna kṛtaḥ panthā vikāle gantum igcchatā
verses.translation: "These pieces of bark have been tied up from above. This may be the path provided as signs by Lakshmana in order to find his way back in odd hours of darkness."

verses.devanagari:
इदम् च उदात्त दन्तानाम् कुन्जराणाम् तरस्विनाम् |
शैल पार्श्वे परिक्रान्तम् अन्योन्यम् अभिगर्जताम्
verses.iast:
idam ca udātta dantānām kunjarāṇām tarasvinām |
śaila pārśve parikrāntam anyonyam abhigarjatām
verses.translation: "At the side of the mountain, this is a roaming place of elephants, having huge teeth, violent as they are and ferociously roaring at each other."

glosses.meaning: at the side of the mountain

verses.devanagari:
यम् एव आधातुम् इग्च्छन्ति तापसाः सततम् वने |
तस्य असौ दृश्यते धूमः सम्कुलः कृष्ट वर्त्मनः
verses.iast:
yam eva ādhātum igcchanti tāpasāḥ satatam vane |
tasya asau dṛśyate dhūmaḥ samkulaḥ kṛṣṭa vartmanaḥ
verses.translation: "See this intense smoke coming from that fire which the sages in the forest always desire to keep in their hermitages."

verses.devanagari:
अत्र अहम् पुरुष व्याघ्रम् गुरु सत्कार कारिणम् |
आर्यम् द्रक्ष्यामि सम्हृष्टो महर्षिम् इव राघवम्
verses.iast:
atra aham puruṣa vyāghram guru satkāra kāriṇam |
āryam drakṣyāmi samhṛṣṭo maharṣim iva rāghavam
verses.translation: "Here, I can see joyfully Rama, the tiger among men, who gives respect to elders and is as venerable as a sage."

verses.devanagari:
अथ गत्वा मुहूर्तम् तु चित्र कूटम् स राघवः |
मन्दाकिनीम् अनुप्राप्तः तम् जनम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
atha gatvā muhūrtam tu citra kūṭam sa rāghavaḥ |
mandākinīm anuprāptaḥ tam janam ca idam abravīt
verses.translation: Proceeding for a while on Chitrakuta mountain and reaching the River Mandakini, that Bharata said to his ministers and others as follows:

glosses.meaning: and reaching mandaakiniim = the River Mandakini
to those people (his ministers and others).

verses.devanagari:
जगत्याम् पुरुष व्याघ्र आस्ते वीर आसने रतः |
जन इन्द्रो निर्जनम् प्राप्य धिन् मे जन्म सजीवितम्
verses.iast:
jagatyām puruṣa vyāghra āste vīra āsane rataḥ |
jana indro nirjanam prāpya dhin me janma sajīvitam
verses.translation: "The foremost of men and the Lord of the people, having sought seclusion, sat on the floor, delighted as he was in the posture of a hero (with his left foot placed on his right knee). O Fie unto my birth and life!"

glosses.meaning: and the Lord of the people
in the posture of a hero (with his left foot placed on his right knee)

verses.devanagari:
मत् कृते व्यसनम् प्राप्तो लोक नाथो महा द्युतिः |
सर्वान् कामान् परित्यज्य वने वसति राघवः
verses.iast:
mat kṛte vyasanam prāpto loka nātho mahā dyutiḥ |
sarvān kāmān parityajya vane vasati rāghavaḥ
verses.translation: "Rama the Lord of Men with great luster, has been overtaken by this misfortune because of me and leaving all enjoyments, is living in the forest."

glosses.meaning: has been overtaken vyasanam = by this msfortune

verses.devanagari:
इति लोक समाक्रुष्टः पादेषु अद्य प्रसादयन् |
रामस्य निपतिष्यामि सीतायाः च पुनः पुनः
verses.iast:
iti loka samākruṣṭaḥ pādeṣu adya prasādayan |
rāmasya nipatiṣyāmi sītāyāḥ ca punaḥ punaḥ
verses.translation: "Thus abhhored by the world, I will fall on the feet of Rama, Seetha and Lakshmana and seek to regain Rama's grace."

verses.devanagari:
एवम् स विलपमः तस्मिन् वने दशरथ आत्मजः |
ददर्श महतीम् पुण्याम् पर्ण शालाम् मनो रमाम्
साल ताल अश्व कर्णानाम् पर्णैर् बहुभिर् आवृताम् |
विशालाम् मृदुभिः तीर्णाम् कुशैर् वेदिम् इव अध्वरे
शक्र आयुध निकाशैः च कार्मुकैर् भार साधनैः |
रुक्म पृष्ठैर् महा सारैः शोभिताम् शत्रु बाधकैः
अर्क रश्मि प्रतीकाशैर् घोरैः तूणी गतैः शरैः |
शोभिताम् दीप्त वदनैः सर्पैर् भोगवतीम् इव
महा रजत वासोभ्याम् असिभ्याम् च विराजिताम् |
रुक्म बिन्दु विचित्राभ्याम् चर्मभ्याम् च अपि शोभिताम्
गोधा अन्गुलित्रैर् आसाक्तैः चित्रैः कान्चन भूषितैः |
अरि सम्घैर् अनाधृष्याम् मृगैः सिम्ह गुहाम् इव
verses.iast:
evam sa vilapamḥ tasmin vane daśaratha ātmajaḥ |
dadarśa mahatīm puṇyām parṇa śālām mano ramām
sāla tāla aśva karṇānām parṇair bahubhir āvṛtām |
viśālām mṛdubhiḥ tīrṇām kuśair vedim iva adhvare
śakra āyudha nikāśaiḥ ca kārmukair bhāra sādhanaiḥ |
rukma pṛṣṭhair mahā sāraiḥ śobhitām śatru bādhakaiḥ
arka raśmi pratīkāśair ghoraiḥ tūṇī gataiḥ śaraiḥ |
śobhitām dīpta vadanaiḥ sarpair bhogavatīm iva
mahā rajata vāsobhyām asibhyām ca virājitām |
rukma bindu vicitrābhyām carmabhyām ca api śobhitām
godhā angulitrair āsāktaiḥ citraiḥ kāncana bhūṣitaiḥ |
ari samghair anādhṛṣyām mṛgaiḥ simha guhām iva
verses.translation: As Bharata was lamenting thus, he beheld in that forest, a splendid and sacred leafy hut, which was covered with many soft leaves of Sala, Tala and Asvakarna trees, overspread with blades of Kusa grass in a sacrificial performance, appearing like an extensive altar and it was adorned with bows plated with gold, like unto the weapons of Indra the Lord of celestials, constructed for heroic exploits, having great power, the torments of their foes, graced with fearful arrows in their quivers, like unto the rays of the sun, bright as serpents with shining hoods, in the same way of Bhagavati (the realm of Nagas), decked with a couple of swords encased in sheaths of gold, adorned with two shields decorated with flowers of gold, finger-guards embroidered with gold and in different colours suspended on walls and which hut was unassailable by hordes of enemies as is a lion's cave to deer.

glosses.meaning: like unto the weapons of Indra the Lord of celestials
like unto the rays of the sun (bright)
in the same way of Bhogavati (the realm of Nagas)

verses.devanagari:
प्राग् उदक् स्रवणाम् वेदिम् विशालाम् दीप्त पावकाम् |
ददर्श भरतः तत्र पुण्याम् राम निवेशने
verses.iast:
prāg udak sravaṇām vedim viśālām dīpta pāvakām |
dadarśa bharataḥ tatra puṇyām rāma niveśane
verses.translation: Bharata saw a sacrificial altar in the north-east corner having a steep descent, extensive in area and having a sacred fire burned in the hermitage of Rama.

verses.devanagari:
निरीक्ष्य स मुहूर्तम् तु ददर्श भरतो गुरुम् |
उटजे रामम् आसीनाम् जटा मण्डल धारिणम्
verses.iast:
nirīkṣya sa muhūrtam tu dadarśa bharato gurum |
uṭaje rāmam āsīnām jaṭā maṇḍala dhāriṇam
verses.translation: Looking around for a moment, Bharata beheld his elder brother, Rama himself seated in the hut, wearing matted locks.

verses.devanagari:
तम् तु कृष्ण अजिन धरम् चीर वल्कल वाससम् |
ददर्श रामम् आसीनम् अभितः पावक उपमम्
सिम्ह स्कन्धम् महा बाहुम् पुण्डरीक निभ ईक्षणम् |
पृथिव्याः सगर अन्ताया भर्तारम् धर्म चारिणम्
उपविष्टम् महा बाहुम् ब्रह्माणम् इव शाश्वतम् |
स्थण्डिले दर्भ सस्म्तीर्णे सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च
verses.iast:
tam tu kṛṣṇa ajina dharam cīra valkala vāsasam |
dadarśa rāmam āsīnam abhitaḥ pāvaka upamam
simha skandham mahā bāhum puṇḍarīka nibha īkṣaṇam |
pṛthivyāḥ sagara antāyā bhartāram dharma cāriṇam
upaviṣṭam mahā bāhum brahmāṇam iva śāśvatam |
sthaṇḍile darbha sasmtīrṇe sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca
verses.translation: Bharata saw that Rama clad in an antelope-skin and robes of bark, seated close by, resembling a fire (in brilliance), with the neck and shoulders of a lion, mighty arms and eyes resembling the lotus, the very virtuous Lord of the Earth extending upto the ocean, the Eternal Brahma, and seated on the ground spread with Darbha grass, with Seetha and Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: with the neck and shoulders of a lion

verses.devanagari:
तम् दृष्ट्वा भरतः श्रीमान् दुह्ख मोह परिप्लुतः |
अभ्यधावत धर्म आत्मा भरतः कैकयी सुतः
verses.iast:
tam dṛṣṭvā bharataḥ śrīmān duhkha moha pariplutaḥ |
abhyadhāvata dharma ātmā bharataḥ kaikayī sutaḥ
verses.translation: Beholding him, the illustrious and the high-souled Bharata the son of Kaikeyim distraught by the grief that possessed him, rushed towards Rama.

glosses.meaning: distraught by the grief that passessed him

verses.devanagari:
दृष्ट्वा च विललाप आर्तो बाष्प संदिग्धया गिरा |
अशक्नुवन् धारयितुम् धैर्याद् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
dṛṣṭvā ca vilalāpa ārto bāṣpa saṃdigdhayā girā |
aśaknuvan dhārayitum dhairyād vacanam abravīt
verses.translation: On seeing his brother, Bharata broke into lamentations and in a voice strangled with sobs, unable to restrain his agony with firmeness, said:

verses.devanagari:
यः संसदि प्रकृतिभिर् भवेद् युक्त उपासितुम् |
वन्यैर् मृगैर् उपासीनः सो अयम् आस्ते मम अग्रजः
verses.iast:
yaḥ saṃsadi prakṛtibhir bhaved yukta upāsitum |
vanyair mṛgair upāsīnaḥ so ayam āste mama agrajaḥ
verses.translation: "My elder brother who is fit to be honoured in an assembly by a body of ministers around him, is now being served by a body of wild beasts around him in this jungle."

verses.devanagari:
वासोभिर् बहु साहस्रैर् यो महात्मा पुर उचितः |
मृग अजिने सो अयम् इह प्रवस्ते धर्मम् आचरन्
verses.iast:
vāsobhir bahu sāhasrair yo mahātmā pura ucitaḥ |
mṛga ajine so ayam iha pravaste dharmam ācaran
verses.translation: "That magnanimous hero, who formerly used to possess countless articles of apparel is now wearing two antelope-skins, following ascetic righteousness.

verses.devanagari:
अधारयद् यो विविधाः चित्राः सुमनसः तदा |
सो अयम् जटा भारम् इमम् सहते राघवः कथम्
verses.iast:
adhārayad yo vividhāḥ citrāḥ sumanasaḥ tadā |
so ayam jaṭā bhāram imam sahate rāghavaḥ katham
verses.translation: "How this Rama, who used to wear various kinds of colourful flowers, is bearing this burden of matted locks now?"

verses.devanagari:
यस्य यज्नैर् यथा आदिष्टैर् युक्तो धर्मस्य संचयः |
शरीर क्लेश सम्भूतम् स धर्मम् परिमार्गते
verses.iast:
yasya yajnair yathā ādiṣṭair yukto dharmasya saṃcayaḥ |
śarīra kleśa sambhūtam sa dharmam parimārgate
verses.translation: "He who acquired merit through countless sacrifices performed according to the prescribed injunctions, now follows the path of righteousness through asceticism!"

glosses.meaning: performed according to the prescribed injunctions

verses.devanagari:
चन्दनेन महा अर्हेण यस्य अन्गम् उपसेवितम् |
मलेन तस्य अन्गम् इदम् कथम् आर्यस्य सेव्यते
verses.iast:
candanena mahā arheṇa yasya angam upasevitam |
malena tasya angam idam katham āryasya sevyate
verses.translation: "He whose body was formerly rendered fragrant by white sandal paste, has only dust with which to smear the limbs of this venerable elder brother!"

verses.devanagari:
मन् निमित्तम् इदम् दुह्खम् प्राप्तो रामः सुख उचितः |
धिग् जीवितम् नृशंसस्य मम लोक विगर्हितम्
verses.iast:
man nimittam idam duhkham prāpto rāmaḥ sukha ucitaḥ |
dhig jīvitam nṛśaṃsasya mama loka vigarhitam
verses.translation: "Rama who used to have happiness, has fallen into this misfortune, because of me cursed be my reprehensive existence that the whole world condemns!"

verses.devanagari:
इत्य् एवम् विलपन् दीनः प्रस्विन्न मुख पन्कजः |
पादाउ अप्राप्य रामस्य पपात भरतो रुदन्
verses.iast:
ity evam vilapan dīnaḥ prasvinna mukha pankajaḥ |
pādāu aprāpya rāmasya papāta bharato rudan
verses.translation: Thus did that pitiable Bharata lament, perspiration be-dewing his lotus-like countenance and, without touching Rama's feet, fell down grooming.

verses.devanagari:
दुह्ख अभितप्तो भरतो राज पुत्रो महा बलः |
उक्त्वा आर्य इति सकृद् दीनम् पुनर् न उवाच किंचन
verses.iast:
duhkha abhitapto bharato rāja putro mahā balaḥ |
uktvā ārya iti sakṛd dīnam punar na uvāca kiṃcana
verses.translation: Overcome with grief, the highly valiant prince Bharata cried out "O, Noble One!" once and in his distress, was unable to speak anything further.

verses.devanagari:
बाष्प अपिहित कण्ठः च प्रेक्ष्य रामम् यशस्विनम् |
आर्य इत्य् एव अभिसम्क्रुश्य व्याहर्तुम् न अशकत् ततः
verses.iast:
bāṣpa apihita kaṇṭhaḥ ca prekṣya rāmam yaśasvinam |
ārya ity eva abhisamkruśya vyāhartum na aśakat tataḥ
verses.translation: Crying at the top of his voice, "O, Noble One" only, on seeing the illustrious Rama, he was unable to speak further, his throat choked with tears.

glosses.meaning: crying at the top of his voice

verses.devanagari:
शत्रुघ्नः च अपि रामस्य ववन्दे चरणौ रुदन् |
ताउ उभौ स समालिन्ग्य रामो अप्य् अश्रूण्य् अवर्तयत्
verses.iast:
śatrughnaḥ ca api rāmasya vavande caraṇau rudan |
tāu ubhau sa samālingya rāmo apy aśrūṇy avartayat
verses.translation: Shatrughna too, weeping, threw himself at Rama's feet and Rama too, embracing them both, allowed his tears to fall.

verses.devanagari:
ततः सुमन्त्रेण गुहेन चैव |
समीयतू राज सुताउ अरण्ये |
दिवा करः चैव निशा करः च |
यथा अम्बरे शुक्र बृहस्पतिभ्याम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ sumantreṇa guhena caiva |
samīyatū rāja sutāu araṇye |
divā karaḥ caiva niśā karaḥ ca |
yathā ambare śukra bṛhaspatibhyām
verses.translation: Then, in that forest, the princes Rama and Lakshmana were seen by Sumantra and Guha, as in the sky, the sun and the moon are seen in conjunction with Venus and Jupiter.

glosses.meaning: and the moon (are seen in conjunction)

verses.devanagari:
तान् पार्थिवान् वारण यूथप आभान् |
समागतामः तत्र महत्य् अरण्ये |
वन ओकसः ते अपि समीक्ष्य सर्वे अप्य् |
अश्रूण्य् अमुन्चन् प्रविहाय हर्षम्
verses.iast:
tān pārthivān vāraṇa yūthapa ābhān |
samāgatāmḥ tatra mahaty araṇye |
vana okasaḥ te api samīkṣya sarve apy |
aśrūṇy amuncan pravihāya harṣam
verses.translation: All those dwellers in the woods, seeing those princes resembling leaders of elephant-herbs meeting together there in that great forest, losing their cheerfulness, began to shed tears.
